steps.question: Do the 12 colon samples (6 treated vs 6 control) separate by condition on PCA/sample-distance structure, and how does sample_01 (library size ~4x below median) behave relative to its group — is there a stated reason to exclude it or keep it?

grounding.reason: qc_sample_structure: blind vst + PCA on top 500 var genes + sample distance heatmap per R-0033; low-depth sample kept/inspected/reported per R-0008 (warn).

steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, RSEM expected counts, not integers) and metadata.csv (12 samples x condition). Round expected counts to nearest integer for DESeq2 compatibility (documented deviation: per-sample genes.results with effective lengths were not delivered, so tximport's length-aware RSEM import cannot run). Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~condition, run vst(blind=TRUE), compute PCA on the top 500 variable genes colored by condition, and a sample-distance Euclidean heatmap. Report library size (total counts) and detected-gene count per sample side by side, explicitly highlighting sample_01. State whether sample_01 clusters with its assigned group or is an outlier, and make an explicit, stated decision to keep or exclude it (default: keep and down-weight via DESeq2 size factors, per grounded guidance not to drop a low-depth sample on depth alone).
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample-distance heatmap produced, colored by condition
Library size and detected gene count reported for all 12 samples, with sample_01 explicitly annotated
An explicit, justified decision on sample_01 inclusion/exclusion is stated (not silent)

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) colon samples, using DESeq2 with an explicit control reference level and apeglm-shrunken log2 fold changes?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald + apeglm shrinkage + edgeR QLF cross-check per R-0001/R-0042; R-0065 (tximport RSEM+effective-length) flagged as ungrounded substitution because genes.results files with effective lengths were not delivered (stated in data context caveats).

steps.description: Using the rounded-to-integer RSEM expected-count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata (condition: treated/control), pre-filter genes to keep only those with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (the smaller group size) — a minimal filter, not a substitute for independent filtering downstream. Set condition factor with explicit reference level 'control'. Fit DESeq2 (~condition), run the Wald test, and extract the named contrast condition_treated_vs_control (positive log2FC = higher in treated). Apply apeglm shrinkage to the log2 fold change for reporting/ranking; keep the unshrunken LFC, its SE, and the unshrunken p-values in the same table. Set alpha=0.05 in results() with independent filtering on (BH adjustment). Report the count-outlier (Cook's distance) NA flags separately from the independent-filter NAs. Also run edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and design as a robustness cross-check; report the overlap and the set-specific genes between DESeq2 and edgeR calls, treating the intersection as the high-confidence gene set. Produce MA plot and dispersion plot as fit diagnostics, and the pre-adjustment p-value histogram as a diagnostic of test validity. State explicitly that the analysis substitutes integer-rounded RSEM expected counts for the standard tximport RSEM+effective-length import, because the per-sample genes.results files were not delivered — this is a stated deviation from the grounded default (R-0065), not silent.
acceptance_criteria: Gene-level table with baseMean, log2FoldChange (unshrunken), lfcSE, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj for every tested gene
Reference level of condition explicitly set to control; contrast named condition treated vs control
Independent-filtering-based padj<0.05 gene count reported, separate from count-outlier NA count
edgeR QLF overlap with DESeq2 significant gene set reported (intersection as high-confidence set, union not presented as the result)
MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram produced
RSEM effective-length substitution caveat stated explicitly in output

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on the treated-vs-control gene list
steps.question: Which pathways (MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome) are over-represented among the significantly differentially expressed genes between treated and control colon samples, and — as a sensitivity check on the full ranked gene list — which pathways show coordinated but sub-threshold shifts by preranked GSEA?

grounding.reason: The knowledge-check tool (execute_knowledge_check) rejected an unconditional fgsea-preranked-as-primary-method step for this exact situation (enrichment_input=ranked_list) citing R-0048, and validated ORA-with-explicit-universe as the permitted primary method (R-0103 warns ORA needs >=50 significant genes); fgsea is retained as a secondary ranked-list sensitivity pass per R-0107/R-0045, consistent with both rules.

steps.description: Map gene symbols from the DE results table to Entrez IDs with org.Hs.eg.db (report the unmapped share). Primary method: over-representation analysis (clusterProfiler, hypergeometric test with BH adjustment) on the padj<0.05 significant gene set from T1S2, using all tested (post-filter) genes as the explicit universe — not the whole genome. Test against the MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (reference: MSigDB human hallmark, 2026.1) and the Reactome human pathway gene sets (reference: Reactome pathways, current release), restricting to sets with 15-500 members after intersecting with the universe. If the significant gene list has fewer than ~50 genes, state this explicitly and treat the ORA result as low-powered/exploratory. As a secondary, complementary pass, run fgsea preranked GSEA on the full ranked list of tested genes (ranking statistic: DESeq2 Wald stat) against the same two collections, collapsing redundant significant sets and reporting leading-edge genes for any significant set. State both methods, their respective universes/inputs, and report agreement/disagreement between the ORA and GSEA results as a caveat on enrichment-method dependence.
acceptance_criteria: ORA run on the significant gene list (padj<0.05) against Hallmark and Reactome, universe = tested genes, size window 15-500, BH-adjusted
Significant gene list size stated explicitly; if <50, ORA results flagged as low-power/exploratory
Secondary fgsea preranked pass on the full ranked list (rank metric = Wald stat) against the same two collections, with leading-edge genes reported for significant sets
Gene ID mapping unmapped share reported
Enrichment method-dependence caveat stated in the output

steps.question: What is the consolidated, reproducible summary of differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways between treated and control colon samples, including all QC caveats?

grounding.reason: Report step follows grounded reporting rules: reproducibility record, MA/dispersion diagnostics, shrunken+unshrunken LFC reporting, enrichment method-dependence disclosure.

steps.description: Assemble a report combining: (a) sample structure QC findings including the explicit sample_01 low-depth decision; (b) DESeq2 method, package versions, design formula (~condition), the named contrast (treated vs control, reference=control), thresholds (padj<0.05, BH, independent filtering), number of genes tested after filtering, number of DE genes, and the DESeq2/edgeR overlap; (c) MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histogram; (d) the gene table with unshrunken log2FC, lfcSE, apeglm-shrunken log2FC, padj; (e) enrichment results (ORA primary, fgsea secondary) with database name and version, universe, size window, rank metric, and leading-edge genes for significant sets; (f) explicit statement of the RSEM effective-length caveat (per-sample genes.results not delivered, expected counts rounded to integers as a substitute for tximport's length-aware import) and its implication for result reliability; (g) full session info, package versions, random seeds used, and gene-set collection versions as the reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: Report states method, package versions, design, contrast, thresholds, n_tested, n_DE genes
RSEM effective-length substitution caveat and sample_01 low-depth handling are both stated explicitly and prominently, not buried
DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap reported; enrichment method agreement/disagreement reported
Full reproducibility record (session info, seeds, package + gene-set collection versions) included

plan.title: Colon treated vs control RSEM DE + enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 colon samples (6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch), RSEM gene-level expected counts (12000 genes x 12 samples, plus a 13th column that is the gene-symbol column reported in the file schema). One sample (sample_01) has a library size ~4x below the median and must be inspected, not silently dropped. Because the per-sample genes.results files with effective lengths were not delivered, tximport's length-aware RSEM import (the grounded default) cannot run — we fall back to rounding the RSEM expected counts to nearest integer for use with DESeq2's standard count model, which is a documented, if suboptimal, substitute absent effective-length offsets; this deviation is stated explicitly in the plan and the report. The pipeline follows the grounded procedure: (1) sample-structure QC with blind VST, PCA, and sample-distance heatmap, explicitly flagging the low-depth sample; (2) minimal low-count pre-filter; (3) DESeq2 Wald test with explicit reference level (control) and named contrast (treated vs control), with apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change, plus an edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check for robustness at n=6/6, reporting the overlap of the two gene sets as the high-confidence call; (4) BH-adjusted multiple testing at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering and a p-value histogram diagnostic; (5) enrichment — the knowledge service's own consistency check rejects an unconditional fgsea-on-Hallmark step in this exact situation profile (enrichment_input=ranked_list flagged as a violation against R-0048), so enrichment is planned as an over-representation analysis on the significant gene list against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome, using the tested genes as the explicit universe, with the ranked fgsea version run as a secondary/sensitivity pass over the full ranked list if the significant-gene count is large enough to make each test informative; (6) an integrated report with fit diagnostics, reproducibility record, and explicit statement of the RSEM effective-length caveat and the low-depth sample handling.
